newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller rejects Yilmaz coalition plan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller rejects Yilmaz coalition plan.

text.p: Turkey's two rival conservative leaders failed on Tuesday to agree on forging a secularist alliance under the leadership of prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz.
"I did not discuss the government issue, so as not to legitimise Yilmaz's position," Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller told reporters after 20 minutes of talks with Yilmaz.
"We said to Yilmaz, 'Go immediately and return the mandate to the president,'" Ciller said.

President Suleyman Demirel on Friday asked Yilmaz to form a government to end months of political turmoil but Ciller, who previously served as Turkey's first woman prime minister, says she should have been nominated for the job.
She said she would offer Yilmaz the chance to join a coalition under her leadership if he failed to cobble together an alliance in the coming days.
"When we get the mandate we will ask Yilmaz to come and join us in a broad-based government," she said

Failing market confidence in the chances of a secularist coalition brought shares back down to earth following a buying spree on Monday fuelled by hopes that Yilmaz was on course to form a new government.

The main Istanbul index closed down 5.07 points. "The market was irritated by the possibility that the (Ciller's) conservative True Path Party may not support the new alliance," said Okan Gulek from Taksim Securities. Shares had soared eight percent on Monday.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, an Islamist, resigned last week after frequent disputes with the army over religious activism.
He now backs a pro-Islamist alliance headed by Ciller, who has served as Erbakan's coalition partner for the last year.

A leftist leader said he would support Yilmaz's secularist grouping, although it is still around a dozen votes short of the simple majority needed to win a confidence vote in the 550-member parliament.
"We are in favour of giving a vote of confidence to the new government," leader Deniz Baykal told a meeting of his Republican People's Party deputies.
The Turkish press says Yilmaz is trying to woo True Path members into his proposed alliance at the expense of Ciller.
